lines.text: One evening, Aarav hears a rumour that a local trust may offer scholarships soon. The old pull returns — a flicker.
But he knows that if he starts hoping again and fails, the disappointment will break him.
If anyone brings me a scholarship form in the next three months, hide it. I need to finish the busy season first. I'll decide in January. Not before.
Precommitment: deliberately restricting your own future choices to protect a clearer decision later. Odysseus binds himself to the mast.
Aarav asks his mother to hide the form. He is not changing his desire. He is managing the timing. This is strategy, not surrender.
